counterfactual_missing_items: absence of systemic symptoms and normal labs
bilateral adrenal enlargement without FDG uptake
decisive_items: Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
An 18 FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake (SUVmax 25.5) in the right testis
no uptake in the adrenal glands
response.rationale: R4 best fits the classic presentation of testicular lymphoma in an elderly man: painless testicular swelling, inhomogeneous ultrasound, intense FDG uptake, and no adrenal uptake despite adrenal enlargement. C1 is a valid anatomical completion of R4 but adds no new evidence. R2 (metastatic cancer) is contradicted by lack of adrenal FDG uptake and absence of systemic symptoms. R5 (primary adrenal hyperplasia) ignores the dominant testicular pathology. R3 (primary adrenal lymphoma) is directly contradicted by no adrenal FDG uptake. R7 (Leydig cell tumor) is less likely given age and very high SUVmax, which favors lymphoma.

rejected.why: Metastatic cancer is unlikely because adrenal lesions show no FDG uptake and there are no systemic symptoms or other metastatic sites.
Primary adrenal macronodular hyperplasia does not explain the testicular mass and intense FDG uptake; adrenal enlargement is likely incidental or reactive.
Primary adrenal lymphoma is contradicted by absent FDG uptake in the adrenal glands and the testicular lesion is the dominant finding.
Leydig cell tumor is less consistent with the patient's age and very high SUVmax; testicular lymphoma is the more common and fitting diagnosis.
